scenarioGroups.observation: The initial attempt failed at Staging Supabase with HTTP 400 while Apple provider was disabled. After owner-approved provider setup, the owner tapped Continue with Apple on the same installed build and reported the browser's Return to CreatorNet page. Tapping Open CreatorNet returned to a signed-in Profile. The owner fully closed and relaunched CreatorNet and reported the profile remained signed in. This is owner-reported happy-path evidence; automatic universal-link return, cancellation, denial, and account variants remain unverified.

The initial attempt failed at Staging Supabase while Google provider was disabled. After Staging-only provider setup, the first completed Google OAuth returned to the app's sign-in choices with a red Could not complete this request error. Staging Auth logs showed Google login, successful admission hook, and HTTP 200 OAuth code exchange. Vercel logged two 503 responses for /api/mobile/profile/me, coinciding with Supabase 400 responses for a 39,078-character /rest/v1/likes URL. After the bounded-batch fix at f639b7e, the owner tapped Try again and reported the Google-signed-in profile appeared. In the fifth gate, the owner fully closed and relaunched the app and reported the Google-signed-in profile persisted; then signed out, started a fresh Google flow, saw Return to CreatorNet, tapped Open CreatorNet, landed on Discover, and opened My Profile. It briefly loaded, then showed the signed-in profile. This supports the Google happy path and cold launch by owner report; automatic universal-link opening, cancellation, denial, and account variants remain unverified.

The owner completed Continue with email using an existing Staging test account on the iPhone and reported that CreatorNet returned to the app signed in. Email address and code were not shared in chat. Invalid/expired code, resend, sign-out, and cold-launch persistence were not tested.

After Apple OAuth, the hosted Return to CreatorNet page appeared and its Open CreatorNet button brought the owner back to the installed app signed in. Google OAuth's first return initially failed profile verification with a server 503; the later hosted fix allowed the existing Google session to show its signed-in profile after Try again. In the fifth gate, fresh Google OAuth reached the Return to CreatorNet page, and Open CreatorNet brought the owner to Discover; My Profile briefly loaded, then showed the signed-in profile. Automatic universal-link handoff, cancel, and failure returns remain unverified.

An earlier email session remained signed in after a devicectl process relaunch by the owner's tentative report. After the later Apple OAuth return, the owner fully closed CreatorNet from the app switcher, relaunched it, opened Profile, and definitively reported the profile still signed in. In the fifth gate, the owner repeated a full close and relaunch with a Google session and again reported the signed-in profile. The owner signed out and saw the sign-in choices before a fresh Google flow. These support cold-launch persistence for Apple and Google and basic logout coherence; token refresh, storage failure and post-logout authorization remain untested.

The installed app initially rendered a 'Couldn't load the feed' screen while the Preview alias was protected. After the owner-approved single-alias exception, a clean app process relaunch rendered the synthetic QA Staging feed on the physical phone. The owner tapped the QA creator avatar, saw the creator profile, and returned to the feed. During the later approved auth gate, the owner opened the signed-in Staging QA buyer profile, and a device screenshot showed its profile identity and three synthetic posts. Authenticated Following and denial cases remain untested. The exact network response behind the initial error was not captured.

The owner tapped the center of the synthetic QA Staging card on the physical phone and reported that media plays. Playback entry is observed by owner report; swipe transitions and captured playback diagnostics are pending.

The owner reported that Join CreatorNet opened the native sign-in page with Continue with email, Continue with Apple, and Continue with Google. Creator profile back navigation returned to the feed. Accessibility, screen size, and failure-state checks remain untested.
